clauses.mechanism: own terms: fixed term of six months from May 9, 1947, effective immediately (month-anniversary computation)
clauses.reason: The sole clause states "hereby suspend for a period of" and, on the next line, "six months, effective immediately, the" eight-hour provisions for the Alaska Railroad work described. The signature date is "May 9,1947" and the filing line reads "Filed, May 9, 1947;", so the suspension began on May 9, 1947 and the six months were complete on November 9, 1947. The recorded end is November 9, 1947 (the later reading); counting May 9 as the first day would make November 8, 1947 the last day of the six months. The proviso that wages be based on a forty-hour administrative workweek with "with overtime to be paid at time and" one-half (the line break follows 'and') is part of the same paragraph and is limited to work under the suspension. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order. The six months are the order's own fixed term, not a report deadline; no later order extends or revokes the suspension, and no held finding of the Secretary of the Interior ends it sooner.

research_rationale:
EO 9849 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9849.txt, 12 FR 3071, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order suspends, for six months from May 9, 1947, the eight-hour-day limit of the act of August 1, 1892 as amended by the act of March 3, 1913 (40 U.S.C. 321) for work by laborers and mechanics of the Alaska Railroad, Department of the Interior, on public work in Alaska that the Secretary of the Interior finds essential, with a proviso on wages and overtime. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The order's own terms fix the period of the suspension.

savings.reason: The proviso required wages of laborers and mechanics to be based on an administrative workweek of forty hours with overtime at time and one-half for hours over forty; wages earned and overtime payable for work done while the suspension was in force are accrued consequences. No held source continues the suspension itself after its six months.
